title: Dashboards: add "Runtime Profiles" overview (profile adoption, latency by profile, kernel fallback)
author: Allison Grant
description: This PR adds a new Grafana dashboard group for the Hardware Tuning Profiles Pack rollout: "Runtime Profiles". The goal is to make profile behavior observable and comparable across SKUs and profile versions during Hosted canary + Dedicated opt-in, with minimal extra cardinality and clear default filters. Dashboard contents: (1) Profile adoption: % traffic by profile_id/profile_version (and sku) over time, with a drilldown table for top model + route combos. (2) Latency by profile: p50/p95/p99 end-to-end latency split by profile_id, and separate panels for scheduler_queue_ms vs compute time to catch regressions due to queueing. (3) Kernel selection + fallback: kernel_choice distribution and kernel_fallback_total rate (normalized by request) by profile_id and model_family, plus a "fallback hotlist" showing top offenders. (4) Safety / headroom signals: KV cache compaction time, fragmentation estimate, and OOM/allocator failure counters tagged with profile_id and sku to correlate stability with profile changes. Notes/assumptions: This expects runtime to export tags {profile_id, profile_version, sku} on the main latency histograms and to export scheduler_queue_ms and kernel fallback counters (see redwood PRs: tag latency with profile_id/sku and export scheduler_queue_ms + kernel_choice/fallback). Where we currently have metric name drift between staging/prod, panels include "OR" selectors and comments to remove once rollout reaches 100%. This PR intentionally does not add paging alerts; we only add dashboard annotations and suggested alert thresholds as panel descriptions to keep the rollout iteration loop fast. Rollout: folder "Serving Runtime" -> subfolder "Profiles". Dashboard is wired into the existing provisioning pipeline (jsonnet) and will appear in staging automatically; prod will follow the next observability-pack deploy. Manual validation steps are in the checklist below. Checklist: [x] Dashboard renders in staging and prod datasources (no missing template vars) [x] Default time range + filters are sane for on-call (last 6h, sku=all, profile_id=all) [x] Panels have clear units and use rate() correctly for counters [x] Top-N tables have hard caps to avoid expensive queries [x] Panel descriptions link to the profile rollout runbook section (Confluence: Profile rollout SLO guardrails) [x] Added a minimal recording rule for expensive queries (fallback rate normalized by requests) to reduce load
commits: dashboards(runtime): add Runtime Profiles overview dashboard (adoption/latency/fallback)
rules: add recording rule for kernel_fallback_rate_per_kreq (perf)
chore: document expected metric tags and links to runtime PRs
conversation: Caleb Johnson (review): Love the overall structure. Two nits: (1) the fallback rate panel uses sum(rate(kernel_fallback_total[5m])) without dividing by requests; can we normalize so it’s comparable across cohorts? (2) template var names should align with the runtime tag spec (profile_id/profile_version/sku).

Allison Grant (author): Good catch. Added a recording rule kernel_fallback_rate_per_kreq = 1000 * fallback_rate / request_rate and swapped the panel to use it. Also renamed the vars to match the runtime spec and updated the panel descriptions with expected labels.
Omar El-Sayed (review): Can we add one panel that correlates fragmentation/compaction with latency? On the incident last week we struggled to see whether p99 was queueing vs allocator churn.

Allison Grant (author): Added a row "Memory / KV cache" with kv_cache_compaction_ms (p95) and kv_cache_fragmentation_estimate (avg) split by profile_id, plus a small correlation table (top routes with highest fragmentation + p99). The queueing vs compute split is already included on the latency row.

Sean Gallagher (review): Please ensure Top-N tables are capped; we’ve had expensive dashboards during incidents. Also, no paging alerts in this PR please—keep it dashboard-only until the SLO guardrails doc is finalized.

Allison Grant (author): Top tables now use topk(15, ...) with hard caps and a default 6h window. No alerts added; only suggested thresholds in panel text. Added a note linking to the rollout SLO guardrails page.
Julian Moore (review): One more: the scheduler queue metric name differs in older builds. Can we make the panel robust with an OR selector and a TODO to remove later?
Allison Grant (author): Done. Panel now uses (scheduler_queue_ms OR runtime_scheduler_queue_ms) with a comment. We can remove once runtime-1.22 is everywhere.
Caleb Johnson (approval): Approved. Recording rule looks good and should help query load.
Omar El-Sayed (approval): Approved—memory row is exactly what we needed.
Sean Gallagher (approval): Approved, thanks for keeping this lightweight for rollout.
release_notes: Added Grafana "Runtime Profiles" dashboard to support hardware tuning profile pack rollout (profile adoption, latency by profile, kernel fallback visibility, KV cache safety signals).
